positions.title: Junior Economist / Policy Analyst - OECD Going Digital - Digital Transformation
positions.description:
As an OECD staff member with the Directors Office & Digital Economy Policy Division of the Directorate for Science, Technology and Innovation, I work on the horizontal project "Going Digital: Making the Transformation Work for Growth and Well-being (Going Digital project)" which was launched in 2017. The project aims to help policy makers better understand the digital transformation that is taking place and develop appropriate policies to help shape a digital future that brings broad benefits and works for all.
My tasks included: 
•	Conducting strategic research and drafting analysis on digital economy policies to support the OECD Going Digital project and digital agendas of G20 and G7
•	Co-authoring key OECD publications: 
‒	"Bridging the Digital Gender Divide: Inlcude, Upskill, Innovate" for G20 Digital Economy Ministers
‒      "The Role of Education and Skills in Bridging the Digital Gender Divide - Evidence from APEC Economies" 
‒	Going Digital Foresight Scenarios for the Strategic Foresight Unit of the OECD General Secretariat
•	Coordinating the OECD Going Digital project, incl. more than 100 sub-projects across 14 multiple OECD Directorates 
•	Coordinating the development of the "Going Digital Toolkit Portal" to assess a country’s level of digital development and help formulating policy strategies
•	Presenting project updates at OECD Committee meetings with more than 250 participants and liaising with international stakeholders

positions.title: Consultant - OECD Innovation Policies for Space and Oceans
positions.description:
I worked primarily for the "Innovation Policies for Space and Oceans" (IPSO) Unit  in the OECD Directorate for Science, Technology and Innovation. “The Future of the Ocean Economy" project was a foresight-oriented project that explores the growth prospects for the ocean economy and its potential for employment creation and innovation. Particular attention is devoted to: the emerging ocean-based industries; the risks and uncertainties surrounding their future development; the innovations required in science and technology; investment needs and environmental impacts; the potential contribution to green growth as well as the negative externalities; the implications for planning and regulation, and the policy options most suited to boost their long-term prospects while managing the ocean in responsible, sustainable ways. 

My tasks with the project involved:
- Conducting quantitative and qualitative research, analysis and preparing substantive outputs, e.g. selected chapters of the final publication “The Ocean Economy in 2030”, continous update and upgrade of the OECD Ocean Economy database and modelling work, country reviews of ocean-based industries, scoping paper on ocean observations, ad-hoc papers to support the ocean team
- Communicating results (outreach) in and outside the Organisation, e.g. presenting the findings on current size and future growth of ocean-based industries at the final symposium in Korea, bilateral meetings with experts on individual ocean-based industries and ocean observation, providing contents for the OECD website and online platforms, presenting findings and output in different OECD bodies
- Providing support for the organization of high-level expert meetings and workshops, e.g. contributing to the drafting of the agenda of OECD workshops, providing ad-hoc logistical support for the workshops, drafting summary records
- Leading and mentoring an effective team of interns and external consultants for the Ocean Economy modelling work

company.name: Max Planck Institute for Innovation and Competition
company.tagline: We are committed to legal and economic research on processes of innovation and competition and their regulation.
company.description:
We are committed to fundamental legal and economic research on processes of innovation and competition and their regulation. Our research focuses on the incentives, determinants and implications of innovation. With an outstanding international team of scholars and excellent scientific and administrative infrastructure including our renowned library, we host academics from all over the world and actively promote young researchers. Through dedicated educational efforts, we engage in the training and mentoring of early-career researchers and foster knowledge exchange with national and international institutions. We inform and guide legal and economic discourse on an impartial basis. As an independent research institution, we provide evidence-based research results to academia, policymakers, the private sector as well as the general public.

In German: Max-Planck-Institut für Innovation und Wettbewerb 

Formerly: Max-Planck-Institut für Immaterialgüter- und Wettbewerbsrecht
Formerly: Max-Planck-Institut für Geistiges Eigentum-, Wettbewerbs- und Steuerrecht
Formerly: Max-Planck-Institut für ausländisches und internationales Patent-, Urheber- und Wettbewerbsrecht
